A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Color3D. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: V1 reports original static and dynamic colorization experiments, component ablations, representation comparisons and a 30-participant user study.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds benchmark evaluations, method-extension experiments, robustness analyses and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: The original per-scene pipeline is retained, but Appendix A.4 adds evaluated extensions: joint training through a shared encoder with scene-specific adapter/decoder routing, and a generalizable transformer colorizer coupled to AnySplat for inference without per-scene optimization. These substantially extend the training and inference procedures.

E1.justification: V2 adds DL3DV-140, also called DL3DV-10-Benchmark, and HyperNeRF to the retained LLFF, Mip-NeRF 360 and DyNeRF evaluations. It also uses COCO to train the feed-forward extension and adds challenging-lighting and Garden-to-Room transfer scenarios.

E2.justification: V2 adds 3DGS/4DGS+VideoColorizer to the main quantitative comparisons, identifying ColorMNet in Section 4.2; v1 evaluated ColorMNet only qualitatively. Appendix Table 5 newly compares against ChromaDistill, and Table 7 includes original 3D/4DGS as runtime comparators. Renaming 2DColorizer to ImageColorizer does not itself change comparator membership.

E3.justification: V2 adds optical-flow-based short- and long-term consistency evaluation, averaging them as TC in existing comparisons. New protocols include BigColor-matched comparisons, one/two/three-key-view controls, and generalizable versus per-scene colorizers using AnySplat. The previously documented splits and standard per-scene training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond retaining v1's component and representation ablations, v2 adds PCA feature-consistency diagnostics, key-view-count and key-view-choice analyses, challenging-lighting examples, and cross-scene transfer failures. These directly examine the consistency mechanism, robustness and generalization boundaries.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or empirical error bars. The aggregate user-study reporting is retained; the new theoretical variance discussion is not experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and ablation values are retained on their original metrics, while v2 adds substantial new results. For example, Table 1 reports DL3DV automatic-colorization FID of 37.48 for Color3D versus 63.56 and 77.89 for image- and video-colorizer baselines. Additional results cover HyperNeRF, TC, ChromaDistill, feed-forward variants, key-view controls and runtime.

T1.justification: New Appendix A.3 introduces Lipschitz and viewpoint-equivariance assumptions, two lemmas, a color-discrepancy proposition, variance and Jacobian arguments, and convergence claims. V1 provides only an intuitive consistency explanation alongside its method equations. The new analysis assumes a consistency-loss term whose use is not established by the retained training description.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution bullets and Section 5 retain the same central claims: controllable static and dynamic 3D colorization through single-view personalization, augmentation and Lab Gaussian reconstruction. The added appendix extensions do not redefine these headline contributions.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations involving feature stability, conflicting supervision from multiple key views, and reduced Gaussian splitting during optimization. It also documents limitations of the generalizable colorizer and color leakage during Garden-to-Room transfer, motivating continued per-scene tuning. V1's original out-of-domain limitation remains in the renumbered limitations section.

D1.justification: V2 adds DL3DV's 960×540 processing resolution, COCO as the extension's training source, a reported 55-minute joint-training time for 140 scenes, and stage-specific runtime measurements. The existing hardware, augmentation recipe, 4K-iteration Adam training, batch size and project-access information are retained; detailed extension hyperparameters remain sparse.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for AnySplat and DL3DV. Bibliography entries for GenN2N and Instruct 4D-to-4D disappear even though those methods remain evaluated. The related-work section and its substantive positioning are otherwise unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main narrative sequence are retained. Changes include limited wording corrections, ImageColorizer terminology, updated author and conference information, and insertion of diagnostic, theoretical and extension sections with corresponding appendix renumbering.

P2.justification: The combined benchmark table becomes separate expanded static and dynamic tables with TC columns. V2 adds feature visualizations, joint-training and feed-forward diagrams, robustness panels, and extension, key-view and timing tables. Existing qualitative galleries and the user-study chart are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens empirical credibility through quantitative ColorMNet and ChromaDistill comparisons, broader coverage, key-view controls and explicit transfer failures, addressing validation gaps in v1. The net gain is limited by theoretical overreach: Appendix A.3 assumes a consistency-loss term absent from the retained Eq. (3) and claims guaranteed view-invariant predictions beyond what its discrepancy bounds establish.
